subject: Request: One-off POC runway + credits for Triton Analytics (exec review)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: One-off POC runway + credits for Triton Analytics (exec review)

Hi team,

Brief background: Triton (contact: Daniel Park) is a top-10 target in our analytics vertical. They signed up through PLG in late April, started a small PoC, and have executed several heavy workload tests in May. Procurement is now asking for a shorter security review and an additional 60 days to complete procurement paperwork — their legal is tied up until mid-July.

Current ask from Triton: extend sandbox access by 60 days and apply a one-off credit of 250k tokens to cover burst evals while procurement finishes PO/contract. Their engineering team is deep into integration and we are seeing strong signal (embedding latency tests, end-to-end inference runs).

Why this matters: Triton has production plans tied to the PoC results (timing-sensitive). If we lose momentum now they'll likely default to a competitor with more permissive trial terms. Standard PLG limits for sandbox trials are 30 days and 100k tokens — this request is non-standard.

Attachments: usage_report_May2028.csv (sample token usage + error-rate curve).

Ask of deal desk/exec: Can we get an exception to grant 60 extra days + 250k complimentary tokens? If not full amount, what's the acceptable uplift we can approve without formal CFO signoff?

Proposed guardrails (my suggested conditional approval if exec agrees):
- Extension active only for the Triton project sub-account; no cross-account reuse.
- Credit expires if Triton doesn’t sign an MSA with PO within 75 days.
- Product/ops to limit concurrent burst to a throttle cap (to protect other tenants).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
[Attachment: usage_report_May2028.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jun 2028 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-off POC runway + credits for Triton Analytics (exec review)

Naomi — thanks for the context and the usage attach. Quick summary from deal desk side: we can approve up to 45 days and 150k tokens programmatically for standard exceptions. Anything above that needs explicit exec sign-off (Rishi). Also need legal to sign off on the expiry guardrail you outlined.

A couple of questions we should confirm before escalation:
1) Does Triton have an OK from procurement to execute a short-form MSA if we extend the sandbox? (if yes — that increases conversion likelihood)
2) Are there any data residency constraints? Triton is US-based but they mentioned EU customers; if data flows are involved we may need security review.

If you can confirm #1 and #2, I’ll tee this up for Rishi’s sign-off with your recommended conditional approval.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Daniel Park <dpark@triton.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jun 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-off POC runway + credits for Triton Analytics (exec review)

Naomi, Marissa — thanks for moving quickly. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement confirmed they can sign our standard SOW once legal has completed a short clause review. They asked for a 60-day runway so legal and budget approvals align.
2) Data residency: current evaluation is US-only. We will surface EU customer data only after an approved contract and separate project.

If it helps, we can sign a short attestation that sandbox credits are only for Triton project usage and will not be shared externally. Happy to add that to a short SOW addendum.

Best,
Daniel Park
Head of Engineering, Triton Analytics
dpark@triton.ai
[Attachment: Triton_SOW_Draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: One-off POC runway + credits for Triton Analytics (exec review)

Thanks everyone for the thread and the usage detail. I reviewed the proposed guardrails. My decision: approve a one-time exception with conditions.

Approval details (executive exception):
- Sandbox extension: 60 calendar days from the approval date (no retroactive extensions).
- Complimentary credits: 200,000 tokens applied to Triton's sandbox account.
- Requirement: Triton signs the SOW addendum (short-form) and returns a PO or signed MSA within 60 days of this approval.
- Security: Limited to US-hosted projects (per Daniel confirmation).
- Monitoring: Product ops to enforce a throttle cap at 3x baseline token/sec to avoid noisy spikes; deal desk will receive weekly usage snapshots until conversion or expiry.

Marissa — please record this in the deal system and add the expiry condition. Naomi — please get Daniel to sign the attestation and the short SOW addendum. Finance/legal notified — any material deviation (larger credit or longer extension) comes back to me.

Appreciate the heads-up — we should consider adding a standard “procurement delay” clause to the PLG flow for 2029 to reduce one-offs.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: One-off POC runway + credits for Triton Analytics (exec review)

Thanks Rishi — that outcome works for Triton. Daniel — can you confirm you'll sign the short addendum and return the SOW + PO within 60 days so we can provision the extension and credits? I’ll have Deal Desk and Product Ops implement the throttle/monitoring and send the first snapshot next week.

Next steps I’ll own:
- Upload SOW addendum to DocuSign (link in related links) and cc procurement.
- Confirm with Product Ops that the credit assignment and throttle are staged by EOD Tuesday.
- Weekly usage snapshot to Marissa and Rishi until conversion.

Appreciate everyone moving quickly — Naomi
